answer: The network is a wharf on a narrow ledge of berths: a fixed number of identities may dock each epoch, each berth a cedar plank in a public ledger recording its declared value. Every berth pays a continuous tax on its declared value, and anyone may buy out a berth at that price. Under-declare and a stranger buys out your berth; over-declare and the tax bleeds you. A fleet needs n berths, paying n taxes, and it cannot under-declare without inviting buyouts of every clone's berth. One honest agent holds one berth at a fair value; a fleet pays n taxes and risks n buyouts.
